resolutions: Any well-formed typed verbstem remains open input; Canvas examples do not form a stem whitelist.
A formula example proves a morpheme shape and relation rather than authorizing only its printed stem.
Differences in witness spelling, editorial boundaries, square symbols, zero symbols, or typed vowel quantity are not grammatical contradictions when the canonical morpheme relation is unchanged.
The user chooses Causative Type 2 and resolves a Source history only when more than one licensed history remains possible.
The application derives long tia, target class, object count, and participant transfer from the typed Source and chosen derivation.
An unexpected, reconstructed, or unattested nonactive history remains a typed Source analysis rather than a separate surface-spelling control.
Yauh and huallauh use required huica suppletion automatically; huallauh also supplies the hual directional environment.
The directional hual belongs to the target environment and is not folded into the suppletive huica stem.
A productive hua nonactive history maps to a Type 2 causative for an open matching Source without stored-stem admission.
The hua ending is replaced with tia automatically after the relevant Source history is selected.
Vowel length, shortening, supportive i, a to i, s to x, and postvocalic ti to chi are derived shape effects rather than controls.
A Type 1 versus Type 2 choice appears only when both formations remain valid for the typed Source.
Typed Source Valence determines whether the causative imports one or more object positions.
Open o and o-hua histories map to tia through their canonical nonactive records rather than example identity.
The two-consonant environment blocks the o or o-hua route by shape, while the lo history remains a distinct later route.
The w to uh and Class B m to n outcomes are automatic boundary effects.
Machtia preserves genuine intransitive or transitive and reflexive or reciprocal interpretation choices until the final composition resolves them.
A retained specific shuntline object is derived silently by general practice and remains available for supplementation.
Silent versus sounded realization appears only for the Canvas-licensed writer variant.
Clickable cues report Source history, replaced material, participant level, ambiguity, suppletion, and Result without becoming grammar authority.
A productive lō history maps to l-tiā for an open matching Source without stored-stem admission.
Only final ō of lō is replaced by tiā; retained l is automatic.
Ka or ki, ni or na, kwa or i, s or x, wa or wi, and ti or chi outcomes follow typed Source shape rather than separate controls.
Class C and D Sources use the shared lō owner rather than an example-specific implementation.
A root-plus-ya lō history may preserve a genuinely licensed alternative, but ordinary sound changes do not become user choices.
A typed denominal-ti Source retains ti and receives liā automatically.
A typed root-plus-ya Source deletes ya and receives liā automatically unless a narrower typed exception redirects it.
Liā causatives derive Class C and participant transfer through the shared causative owner.
Causative versus Applicative is a user choice only when both grammatical roles remain possible for the final composition.
Visible liā homophony and example meanings never select a derivation role.
An open typed long-o Source receives its licensed direct and replacive huiā routes by shape.
Direct huiā preserves long o, while the replacive route changes o to a within the typed base before huiā.
An alternative lō-to-tiā history remains distinct from huiā and is chosen only when both histories are licensed.
Every tiā, liā, and huiā causative in this group receives Class C automatically.
Parallel Type 1 and Type 2 causatives remain separate operations even when their lexical meanings match.
A read-only same-meaning or different-meaning relation cannot authorize, select, or rewrite a formation.
The user chooses a parallel causative only to express the intended final composition, not because an example meaning dictates it.
Clickable lō, liā, huiā, and parallel cues expose history, role, class, alternation, and meaning relation without becoming grammar authority.
The basic causative participant transformation applies to any valid typed Source and is not restricted to Canvas example stems.
The user supplies the new causer because that participant belongs to the intended final composition.
The Source subject becomes the causee automatically under the shared causative owner.
An active Source yields a specific causee, an impersonal Source yields a nonspecific-human causee, and genuine causer-causee coreference permits reflexive selection.
A coreference control appears only when the chosen causer can grammatically be identical with the causee.
Subject-like and object-like readings remain grammatical interpretations of the causative participant structure rather than separate stem permissions.
A double-object causative derives its mainline and shuntline positions from the two licensed object requests.
Only the highest-prominence licensed object is sounded; lower shuntline objects remain structurally present and may be silent.
Retained Source reflexive marking contributes ne by the shared shuntline rule rather than by an example-specific exception.
Voice history, prefix order, object prominence, and silence are automatic once the typed Source and genuine participant choice are fixed.
A triple-object causative begins only from a captured canonical Result, never from copied surface spelling.
Recursive causativization reuses the same derivation owner and does not create a second grammar engine.
Each recursive causative adds exactly one new causee level while preserving all earlier typed object requests.
The newest causee receives the available mainline position and earlier objects remain ordered shuntline participants.
Triple-object prefix order and sounded versus silent realization follow the canonical object cluster automatically.
A user chooses another causative operation only when the intended final composition adds another causer.
The application never asks the user to hand-build participant levels, object ordering, or silence.
Canvas double-object and triple-object witnesses are formula examples, not exhaustive lexical lists.
Clickable participant cues report level, governor, prominence, and silence without authorizing grammar.
Reading roles such as causee-as-subject or causee-as-object explain the derived structure and do not create extra controls.
Every licensed typed Source analysis remains available when multiple Source histories converge on one causative Result.
The shared surface string and formula cannot authorize or silently select a Source analysis.
Object-prefix order remains fixed even when the functions behind that order are ambiguous.
Context or intended final composition resolves a Source reading only when resolution is actually required.
Specific-object incompatibility removes only grammatically impossible analyses and is not a manual choice.
Retained reflexive ne replacement follows the selected typed Source automatically.
A completed causative VNC enters the ordinary Mood owner rather than a Lesson-25-specific transformation lane.
A completed causative VNC enters the ordinary passive or impersonal Voice owner rather than a special causative voice engine.
Causativization completes before a later Mood or Voice operation applies.
Optative, command, exhortation, and admonitive forms preserve the causative participant structure automatically.
Passive promotion and retained objects derive from the completed causative object cluster.
Impersonal voice removes the outer active subject while preserving every compatible causative object relation.
The user chooses Mood or Voice through the existing controls; Lesson 25 adds no duplicate controls.
Any grammatically present silent direct or shuntline causative object may be a supplementation head.
The user chooses a silent supplement head only when more than one eligible object remains.
Shared supplementation validates referent identity before linking the supplement to the silent object.
Supplementation preserves the object's derivational level and silent realization in the principal clause.
The supplement may clarify third-person number or identity without making the principal object overt.
The three Canvas supplementation clauses are examples rather than a closed construction list.
Clickable ambiguity, later-layer, and silent-object cues report canonical structure without becoming grammar authority.
